Windows 8.1 Calculator app

A Metro-style app that shows the grammar at small scale: gray key tiles, thin numerals, and one green key.

Context

Commons describes it as “Windows 8.1’s additional Metro-style calculator app in standard mode”.

Microsoft published the Windows Calculator source under the MIT License in 2019 (microsoft/calculator, repository created 28 January 2019).

Observed

  • The ground is a flat charcoal. Three mode names at top (Standard, Scientific, Converter) are thin type; the active one is white and the others gray.
  • The display is a slightly lighter gray panel with a thin green line along its top edge and a very thin, very large white “0” at right.
  • Keys are flat mid-gray rectangles with square corners, separated by narrow dark gaps. Digits and operators are thin white or gray glyphs.
  • The equals key is the only color: a solid green rectangle with a white sign.
  • A separate column of memory and function keys is set apart by a wider gap, not by a line.

Why it belongs

It shows how Metro handles a dense control surface with almost no color: one hue marks the primary action, and space groups the rest.

Borrow

In a dense control grid, keep every key the same neutral fill and give only the primary action a saturated color.

Group controls with a wider gap instead of a rule or box.
